Subject: Securing computational memory IP ahead of Samsung production

Jin,

Congrats on the $570M valuation. As XCENA moves the MX1 from prototype to Samsung foundry production at end 2026, your computational memory architecture patents are entering a critical filing window.

The IP space around compute-in-memory (CXL-based, RISC-V cores within DRAM) is rapidly becoming contested — Astera Labs, Marvell, and memory giants like Samsung and SK Hynix are all investing heavily in overlapping areas.

For companies at the nexus of custom silicon and hyperscaler infrastructure, a comprehensive IP strategy typically covers:
- Compute-in-memory methodology claims
- CXL-based data orchestration architecture
- Memory-level KV cache management innovations
- Cross-border IP considerations for Korean HQ / US market sales

We published an AI Patent Strategy Scorecard that walks through these and 11 other critical gaps in compute-hardware IP portfolios. Worth a look as you finalize your production timeline.

Educational content only — not legal advice. Attended for attorney review.
